schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE Examination
(
    ID                 INTEGER          null,
    `Examination Date` DATE         null,
    `aCL IgG`          REAL        null,
    `aCL IgM`          REAL        null,
    ANA                INTEGER          null,
    `ANA Pattern`      TEXT null,
    `aCL IgA`          INTEGER          null,
    Diagnosis          TEXT null,
    KCT                TEXT null,
    RVVT              TEXT null,
    LAC                TEXT null,
    Symptoms           TEXT null,
    Thrombosis         INTEGER          null,
    foreign key (ID) references Patient (ID)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE Patient
(
    ID           INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    SEX          TEXT  null,
    Birthday     DATE          null,
    Description  DATE          null,
    `First Date` DATE          null,
    Admission    TEXT  null,
    Diagnosis    TEXT  null
);

CREATE TABLE Laboratory
(
    ID        INTEGER  default 0            not null,
    Date      DATE default '0000-00-00' not null,
    GOT       INTEGER                       null,
    GPT       INTEGER                        null,
    LDH       INTEGER                        null,
    ALP       INTEGER                        null,
    TP        REAL             null,
    ALB       REAL             null,
    UA        REAL             null,
    UN        INTEGER                       null,
    CRE       REAL             null,
    `T-BIL`   REAL             null,
    `T-CHO`   INTEGER                       null,
    TG        INTEGER                       null,
    CPK       INTEGER                       null,
    GLU       INTEGER                       null,
    WBC       REAL             null,
    RBC       REAL             null,
    HGB       REAL             null,
    HCT       REAL             null,
    PLT       INTEGER                       null,
    PT        REAL             null,
    APTT      INTEGER                       null,
    FG        REAL             null,
    PIC       INTEGER                       null,
    TAT       INTEGER                       null,
    TAT2      INTEGER                       null,
    `U-PRO`   TEXT              null,
    IGG       INTEGER                       null,
    IGA       INTEGER                       null,
    IGM       INTEGER                       null,
    CRP       TEXT              null,
    RA        TEXT              null,
    RF        TEXT              null,
    C3        INTEGER                       null,
    C4        INTEGER                       null,
    RNP       TEXT              null,
    SM        TEXT              null,
    SC170     TEXT              null,
    SSA       TEXT              null,
    SSB       TEXT              null,
    CENTROMEA TEXT              null,
    DNA       TEXT              null,
    `DNA-II`  INTEGER                       null,
    primary key (ID, Date),
        foreign key (ID) references Patient (ID)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

First, I'll look at the two queries. Both are counting patients (T1.ID from Patient) joined with Laboratory (T2) on ID. The WHERE clauses both have T1.SEX = 'F' and T2.WBC < 3.5. The difference is that Q1 uses COUNT(T1.ID) while Q2 uses COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID). 

Wait, but in an INNER JOIN, each row from Patient will be matched with each row from Laboratory that has the same ID. So if a patient has multiple entries in the Laboratory table (since the primary key is (ID, Date)), then joining would produce multiple rows for the same patient. 

In Q1, COUNT(T1.ID) counts all those rows, potentially counting the same patient multiple times. Q2 uses COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID), which counts each patient once regardless of how many lab entries they have. So they are not equivalent unless each patient has exactly one lab entry. 

To create a counterexample, I need a scenario where a female patient has multiple lab records with WBC < 3.5. Then Q1 would count each lab record (so higher number), while Q2 counts the distinct patient once. 

Let's set up two patients. Patient 1 (ID=1, SEX='F') has two lab entries with WBC < 3.5. Patient 2 (ID=2, SEX='F') has one lab entry with WBC < 3.5. Then Q1 would count 3 (2 from patient 1, 1 from patient 2), and Q2 would count 2 (distinct patients). 

Wait, but in the schema, Laboratory has a composite primary key of (ID, Date). So each patient can have multiple lab records on different dates. So inserting two lab records for the same patient with different dates but same ID would work. 

So the counterexample would have two female patients. One has two lab entries with WBC < 3.5, the other has one. Then Q1 gives 3, Q2 gives 2. Hence, they are not equivalent.
